remarks: No tracked port carries a weather or closure entry this run, and none carried one last run either. Nothing in the set is suspended or recovering from a storm.

Dujuan is the only active system in the basin and it is no longer a container-port story at all. It has moved from 32.3N 138.3E to 37.2N 145.9E since the 21 September read, running northeast at 45 km/h into open water east of Japan, and its closest approach to any tracked port has widened from 911 km to 1,530 km at Busan. The forecast track out to +24h only widens it further. No threat rows are written.

The queues at Shanghai, Ningbo and Yantian are still large but they are not a weather event. Saudel and Krovanh dissipated in early September; what is left is backlog plus the cargo rush ahead of Golden Week on 1 October. Those ports are deliberately kept out of the port list so the site's own idle-berth flag is not suppressed — the congestion data speaks for itself here.

One scheduled stoppage worth knowing about but deliberately not recorded as a port entry: Busan terminals halt for 24 hours from 25 to 26 September for Chuseok. That is a public holiday, not an extraordinary disruption, and writing it as suspended would both mislead and block the site's automatic removal rules.
